Prealgebra · Lesson 4.6

Adding and Subtracting Fractions

Solve this lesson →All lessons

A robot at 00 steps a third of the way to 11, then half of the way, and stops past the middle. It is tempting to add the tops and add the bottoms and read off the landing spot, but the two steps are different lengths, and that breaks the shortcut. Adding fractions is stepping right along the line and subtracting is stepping left. Either way the counting only works when both steps are built from the same size piece, so when they are not, you rebuild them until they are.

Problem
A counter on a strip notched into ninths slides right 22 notches, then 55 more. Every notch is the same width. What is 29+5992​+95​, written as a fraction?
Show a hint
  • The two slides are made of the same ninth-sized notches, so you never have to change the notch size partway through. You only need to count how many of those equal notches the counter has crossed by the end.
  • Add the number of notches, 2 then 5, to get the total notches crossed, and keep the notch size the same. That total goes on top, and the 9 that names the notch size stays on the bottom.
Show the full solution
The notches are all the same width, so just count them. Two notches then five more is 2+5=72+5=7 notches, and each notch is 1991​ of the strip. So 29+59=7992​+95​=97​, which is 7/97/9​. The 9 on the bottom names the size of one notch, and that size does not change as the counter slides, so only the count on top moves.
Problem
A marker at 7887​ steps left by 3883​. Count remaining eighth-notches, then reduce. What is 78−3887​−83​ in simplest form?
Show a hint
  • Both fractions are built from the same eighth-sized notches, so subtracting them is really just counting notches. Start at 7 notches and step back 3. How many notches remain, and over what bottom number?
  • Seven eighths minus three eighths leaves 4884​. Now do not stop there. The top is 4 and the bottom is 8, and they share a factor of 4. Divide both by 4 and write what you get.
Show the full solution
Both fractions count eighth-sized notches, so start at 7 notches and step back 3. That leaves 7−3=47−3=4 notches, so 78−38=4887​−83​=84​. Top and bottom both divide by 4, which gives 1/21/2​. A sum or difference often is not in simplest form yet, so check for a shared factor before you stop. Landing on the fourth notch out of eight is the halfway point, which confirms it.
Key idea
Same denominator, add the numerators. When two fractions are built from the identical piece, the bottom number only says how big one piece is. That size does not change when you add or remove pieces, so you add or subtract the tops (the count of pieces) and copy the bottom down unchanged. Never add the bottoms, since you are totaling pieces, not sizes. Then check the result, because a sum or difference is often not in simplest form yet, which is why 78−3887​−83​ simplifies to 1221​.
Problem
A friend adds 13+12=2531​+21​=52​ (tops and bottoms). But 25<1252​<21​, less than one step. Find the correct sum 13+1231​+21​ over the lcd.
Show a hint
  • The two fractions are different sizes, so you cannot add them yet. Find a denominator that both 3 and 2 fit into evenly. The smallest one is the lcd of 2 and 3.
  • The lcd is 66. Rename each fraction over 6, since the pieces have to match before you count them: 13=2631​=62​ and 12=3621​=63​. Now the denominators agree, so keep the 66 on the bottom and add only the top numbers.
Show the full solution
The lcd of 22 and 33 is 66, so rewrite both over sixths. 13=2631​=62​ and 12=3621​=63​. Now the steps are the same size, so add the counts, 2+3=52+3=5, giving 26+36=5/662​+63​=5/6​. Stacking tops and bottoms fails because a third and a half are different sizes. You can only add counts of pieces that match.
Key idea
Never add the denominators. Adding tops and bottoms together gives the wrong answer. It treats a half and a third as the same size when they are not, so the result is not the sum. The bottom is a size name, not something you count, so you never add it. To add two fractions, first rebuild both from pieces that match, which is all a common denominator does. Once 1221​ and 1331​ are both rewritten as a number of equal sixths, you are back to plain counting.
Problem
A glider burns 1441​ then 1661​ of a charge. Find lcm⁡(4,6)lcm(4,6), rewrite, add. How much burned total? Write in simplest form.
Show a hint
  • You can only add numerators once the bottoms match, so first find the lcd of 44 and 66. The smallest number both divide into is 1212. Now think about what each fraction becomes when its denominator is 1212.
  • Use the build-up move from 4.4. Since 4×3=124×3=12, multiply top and bottom of 1441​ by 33 to get 312123​. Since 6×2=126×2=12, multiply top and bottom of 1661​ by 22 to get 212122​. Add the numerators over the common bottom 1212, then check whether the result can be reduced.
Show the full solution
The lcd of 44 and 66 is 1212. Since 4×3=124×3=12, 14=31241​=123​, and since 6×2=126×2=12, 16=21261​=122​. Both are twelfths now, so add the tops, 3+2=53+2=5. The glider burned 5/125/12​ of a charge. Since gcd⁡(5,12)=1gcd(5,12)=1, that is already in simplest form.

Nothing about subtraction is new. If adding is a step right along the line, subtracting is a step left, and the rule about sizes is the same whichever way you walk. You still cannot count pieces until they match, so a difference takes the same three moves as a sum. Match the sizes, count the pieces, simplify. The next problem is 56−3865​−83​.

Problem
Timer is 5665​ used, and a shortcut saves 3883​. Find lcm⁡(6,8)lcm(6,8), rename, subtract. Find 56−3865​−83​ in simplest form.
Show a hint
  • The two slices are different sizes, so first give them a common bottom. List multiples of 66 and of 88 and find the smallest number both reach. That smallest shared multiple is your lcd, and every sixth and every eighth can be re-cut into pieces of that size.
  • The lcd is 2424. Rename 56=202465​=2420​ since 6×4=246×4=24 and 5×4=205×4=20, and rename 38=92483​=249​ since 8×3=248×3=24 and 3×3=93×3=9. Now the bottoms match, so subtract the tops: 20−920−9 over 2424. Check whether the result can be reduced.
Show the full solution
The multiples of 88 are 8,16,248,16,24, and 2424 is the first one 66 also reaches, so the lcd is 2424. Rename both. Since 6×4=246×4=24, 56=202465​=2420​, and since 8×3=248×3=24, 38=92483​=249​. Subtract the tops, 20−9=1120−9=11, so 56−38=11/2465​−83​=11/24​. The number 1111 is prime and does not divide 2424, so the answer is already in lowest terms.
Key idea
The three-step rule. Adding or subtracting fractions is always the same three steps in the same order. First give both fractions the same denominator, which means finding the least common denominator and renaming each fraction. Counting only works when every piece is the same size. Second, add or subtract the numerators and keep the shared denominator, since the number of pieces changes but the size of a piece does not. Third, check whether the numerator and denominator still share a factor, and reduce if they do.
Problem
Mixer pours 512125​ then 1441​. The lcd is 1212. Add the tops, then reduce, since the sum shares a factor. What fraction was poured in simplest form?
Show a hint
  • The lcd of 1212 and 44 is 1212, since 1212 is already a multiple of 44. The 512125​ is fine as is. Rename 1441​ so its bottom is 1212 by multiplying top and bottom by 33.
  • You should have 512+312=812125​+123​=128​. That is correct but not reduced. Both 88 and 1212 divide by 44, so split both by 44 to land on your final fraction.
Show the full solution
Since 1212 is already a multiple of 44, the lcd is 1212 and only 1441​ needs renaming. Multiply its top and bottom by 33 to get 312123​, then add over the shared bottom, 512+312=812125​+123​=128​. Both 88 and 1212 divide by 44, so the mixer poured 2/32/3​ of the can. When one denominator is already a multiple of the other, that one is the lcd and only one fraction has to be recut.
Fun fact
The ++ sign appeared in European arithmetic in the late 1400s, likely from writing the Latin et ("and"). The fraction bar is older, from Arabic c. 1100s.
Problem
Dial reads 3883​. Stepping left by 5665​ crosses 00. Common denominator, subtract in order, keep the sign. What is 38−5683​−65​ in simplest form?
Show a hint
  • The two denominators are 88 and 66. Their least common denominator is 2424, since 2424 is the smallest number both 88 and 66 divide into. Rewrite each fraction with 2424 on the bottom before you try to subtract anything.
  • Multiply top and bottom of 3883​ by 33 to get 924249​, and multiply 5665​ by 44 to get 20242420​. Now the subtraction is 924−2024249​−2420​. Since 99 is smaller than 2020, the count 9−209−20 comes out negative. Work out 9−209−20, keep it over 2424, and check whether the result can be reduced.
Show the full solution
The lcd of 88 and 66 is 2424. Rename each fraction, 38=92483​=249​ and 56=202465​=2420​. Taking 2020 twenty-fourths away from only 99 of them drops the count below zero, 9−20=−119−20=−11, so 38−56=−11/2483​−65​=−11/24​. Order matters in a subtraction. The dial walks left past 00 and stops on the negative side of the same line you used in 4.1.
Key idea
Signs, whole numbers, and long sums. A difference can be negative. Subtract more than you started with and the result drops below 00, so 38−5683​−65​ is the opposite of 56−3865​−83​. Order matters, so keep track of the sign. A whole number can be written as n11n​, and a sum of three or more fractions goes over one shared lcd all at once. Adding numerators does not tell you whether the answer is reduced, so the last step is always to look for a shared factor.
Problem
Spool holds 44 m. Cut 2332​ m off. Rewrite 4=1234=312​, subtract. How much cord remains? Find 4−234−32​ as a single fraction.
Show a hint
  • You cannot take thirds away from something that is still written in whole meters. First turn the 44 into thirds. Since 4=414=14​ and you want a denominator of 33, multiply the top and bottom by 33. How many thirds are in 4 whole meters?
  • Four whole meters is 4×31×3=1231×34×3​=312​, so you have 12 thirds on the spool. Now both amounts are measured in the same size pieces, and the subtraction becomes 123−23312​−32​. Keep the denominator and subtract the tops, 12−212−2.
Show the full solution
Write the whole number as a fraction and give it thirds, 4=41=4×31×3=1234=14​=1×34×3​=312​, since each meter holds 33 thirds. Both amounts are in thirds now, so 123−23=103312​−32​=310​, and 10/310/3​ of a meter is left. Any whole number is already a fraction over 11, which is all you need to rename it over any denominator.
Problem
Spring: 3443​ planted, path takes 2332​, 1661​ replanted. Find lcd for 4,3,64,3,6, combine in one sweep. What fraction ends up in use?
Show a hint
  • The smallest number that 44, 33, and 66 all divide into is 1212. Rewrite every fraction with 1212 on the bottom before you touch the top numbers, and keep the plus and minus signs attached to the right pieces.
  • Over 1212 the three fractions are 912129​, 812128​, and 212122​. The expression 34−23+1643​−32​+61​ becomes 9−8+212129−8+2​. Work left to right on top, then simplify the fraction you get.
Show the full solution
All of 44, 33, and 66 divide 1212, so put every fraction over 1212. That gives 34=91243​=129​, 23=81232​=128​, and 16=21261​=122​, so the expression becomes 9−8+212=312.129−8+2​=123​. Divide top and bottom by 33, and 1/41/4​ of the plot ends up in use. Converting all three at once and then sweeping the top left to right keeps each sign attached to its own number.
Problem
Rider: +710−15+12+107​−51​+21​. lcd for 10,5,210,5,2 is 1010. Combine in one pass. What fraction of the loop is her total progress?
Show a hint
  • You need one denominator that all three fractions can share. Ask yourself the smallest number that 1010, 55, and 22 all divide into evenly. Since 55 and 22 both already divide 1010, that shared denominator is just 1010.
  • Rewrite each fraction over 1010. The first is already 710107​. For 1551​, multiply top and bottom by 22 to get 210102​. For 1221​, multiply top and bottom by 55 to get 510105​. Now combine the numerators in order, keeping the minus sign on the second one, so 7−2+57−2+5 over 1010.
Show the full solution
Both 55 and 22 divide evenly into 1010, so 1010 is already the lcd. Rename the other two terms, 15=21051​=102​ and 12=51021​=105​, then combine the tops in one pass with their signs, 7−2+5=107−2+5=10. That is 10101010​, one full loop, so her progress is 11​. Check the denominators you already have before hunting for a new one, since the largest is often the lcd.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A counter on a sevenths number line steps right 1771​ then 3773​. Count the notches. Write 17+3771​+73​ in simplest form.
Show the solution
The bottoms already match, so just count notches. One notch then 33 more is 1+3=41+3=4 sevenths, so 17+37=4/771​+73​=4/7​. Since gcd⁡(4,7)=1gcd(4,7)=1, nothing cancels.
Practice
A counter at 910109​ slides left by 310103​. Subtract and reduce. What is 910−310109​−103​ in simplest form?
Show the solution
Both fractions count tenths, so the subtraction happens only on top. 9−3=69−3=6, giving 910−310=610109​−103​=106​. Divide top and bottom by 22 to get 3/53/5​. Same-size pieces subtract straight across, but the result still needs a simplicity check.
Practice
A classmate wrote 13+14=2731​+41​=72​ by stacking tops and bottoms. But 27<1372​<31​, so a sum came out smaller than a part, which is impossible. Find the correct sum over the lcd, in simplest form.
Show the solution
The lcd of 33 and 44 is 1212. Rename both, 13=41231​=124​ and 14=31241​=123​, then add the tops, 4+3=74+3=7. The correct sum is 7/127/12​. Stacking tops and bottoms treats thirds and fourths as the same size, which is how it produced a sum smaller than one of the parts.
Practice
"Sunset" blend: 2552​ mango, 1331​ pineapple. Find lcm⁡(5,3)lcm(5,3), rename, add. Total fruit share 25+1352​+31​ in simplest form?
Show the solution
The lcd of 55 and 33 is 1515. Rename each share, 25=61552​=156​ and 13=51531​=155​, then add the tops, 6+5=116+5=11. The blend is 11/1511/15​ fruit by volume. Since 1111 is prime and does not divide 1515, that is already in lowest terms.
Practice
A candle is 7887​ of its original height, and it burns 1331​ more. Find the lcd of 88 and 33, rename, subtract. What is 78−1387​−31​ in simplest form?
Show the solution
The denominators 88 and 33 share no factor, so the lcd is their product, 8×3=248×3=24. Rename both, 78=212487​=2421​ and 13=82431​=248​, then subtract the tops, 21−8=1321−8=13. The candle keeps 13/2413/24​ of its original height. When two denominators share no common factor, multiplying them always gives the lcd.
Practice
A bottle is 710107​ full, and the hiker drinks 1221​ of a bottle. Find the lcd, rename, subtract. What fraction of a bottle is left, in simplest form?
Show the solution
Since 1010 is already a multiple of 22, the lcd is 1010 and only the half gets renamed, 12=51021​=105​. Subtract the tops, 7−5=27−5=2, giving 210102​. Both divide by 22, so 1/51/5​ of a bottle is left. A correct difference is not always reduced, so hunt for a shared factor last.
Practice
A probe is at +16+61​ then sinks by 3443​, crossing 00. Compute 16−3461​−43​ over a common denominator. What is the result, with sign, in simplest form?
Show the solution
The lcd of 66 and 44 is 1212. Rename each one, 16=21261​=122​ and 34=91243​=129​, then subtract the tops, 2−9=−72−9=−7. The reading is −7/12−7/12​. The probe started only 22 twelfths above zero and dropped 99, so it ends below the surface and the answer comes out negative.
Practice
A pitcher holds 55 cups, and 2332​ of a cup is added. Rewrite 5=515=15​ over denominator 33, then combine. Find 5+235+32​ as a single fraction.
Show the solution
Write the whole number as 5=515=15​, then multiply top and bottom by 33 to get 153315​. Both amounts are thirds now, so add the tops, 15+2=1715+2=17. The pitcher holds 17/317/3​ cups. Since 1717 is prime and shares no factor with 33, nothing cancels.
Practice
A ribbon is 22 m, and 3883​ m is cut off. Rewrite 2=212=12​ over eighths, then subtract. What is 2−382−83​ as a single fraction?
Show the solution
Write 2=212=12​, then multiply top and bottom by 88 to get 168816​, because 1616 eighths really is two whole meters. Subtract the tops, 16−3=1316−3=13, so 2−38=13/82−83​=13/8​ of a meter. That is a little over one and a half meters, which fits, since only a small piece was cut off.
Practice
Three bursts: 12+14+1821​+41​+81​ of a fuel cell. lcd for 2,4,82,4,8 is 88. Total fraction used, in simplest form?
Show the solution
Both 22 and 44 divide 88, so 88 works for all three fractions at once. Rename, 12=4821​=84​, 14=2841​=82​, and 1881​ is already there, then add the tops in one sweep, 4+2+1=74+2+1=7. The bursts use 7/87/8​ of a cell. With three fractions you never combine them in pairs. Put them all over one denominator and add once.
Practice
Kite: +12+13−15+21​+31​−51​. lcd for 2,3,52,3,5 is 3030. How far above ground, in simplest form?
Show the solution
The denominators 22, 33, and 55 are primes with nothing in common, so the lcd is their product, 2×3×5=302×3×5=30. Rename each move, 12=1530,13=1030,15=630,21​=3015​,31​=3010​,51​=306​, then combine the tops with their signs, 15+10−6=1915+10−6=19. The kite sits 19/3019/30​ of the way to the marker. Here the lcd is the product of the denominators, not simply the largest one.
Practice
A tank starts 11121211​ full, and pipes draw 1221​ then 1441​. Find 1112−12−141211​−21​−41​ over the lcd. What fraction remains, in simplest form?
Show the solution
Twelve is a multiple of 22 and of 44, so put everything over 1212. The 11121211​ stays, 12=61221​=126​, and 14=31241​=123​, so the chain reads 1112−612−3121211​−126​−123​. Sweep the tops in one go, 11−6−3=211−6−3=2, giving 212122​. Divide both by 22, so 1/61/6​ of the tank remains.
